answer:
Fix alert noise first, not the rotation. 1-in-6 weekly is a healthy schedule; ~10 pages/wk mostly false is the problem.

1. **Audit last 4-8 wks of pages.** Tag each: actionable / false / duplicate / self-resolved. Expect 2-3 alerts to cause most of the volume.
2. **Delete or demote the top offenders.** Rule: a page must mean user-visible impact + human action needed now. Everything else goes to a ticket or Slack channel, reviewed in business hrs.
3. **Tune what remains.** Add duration windows (e.g., fire only if sustained 5+ min), dedupe/group related alerts, page on symptoms (error rate, latency, SLO burn) not causes (CPU, disk, single-host restarts).
4. **Auto-remediate repeats.** If the runbook is "restart X", script it.
5. **Keep it fixed.** Weekly 15-min handoff review of every page; the on-call engineer has authority to kill or fix any alert that fired falsely. Reserve part of on-call week for this work, not feature work.

Target: ≤2 pages/wk, >80% actionable. Track both numbers.

Interim relief while cleaning up: comp time after any night page, and split off-hrs paging to only the critical-severity subset.
